cities.name: New York

seo.title: Where to meet in New York
seo.description: Sample guide: places in New York that work for groups, from coffee catch-ups to team meetings, plus how to get around by subway.

cities.intro:
*Sample copy for local development. The real intro comes from the control plane.*

New York is easy to reach and hard to agree on. A group spread across Brooklyn, Queens and Manhattan can spend longer choosing a place than getting there. These guides collect places that work for common plans, chosen so most people can arrive on one subway line.

Pick the kind of plan below, or start with a neighborhood.
cities.transit_notes:
*Sample copy.* Most trips here are by **subway**. A place within a short walk of a station served by several lines, like Union Square or Times Square, is usually the most convenient pick for a mixed group.

- Check weekend service changes before you send the plan.
- Allow extra time for crossing between boroughs at rush hour.

seo.title: Coffee shops for a catch-up near Union Square
seo.description: Sample guide: coffee shops a few minutes from Union Square for two friends catching up, close to subway lines from every borough.

guides.intro:
*Sample copy for local development.*

A coffee catch-up should take an hour, not an afternoon of travel. Union Square sits on a handful of subway lines, so two friends coming from Brooklyn, Queens or the Upper West Side can usually get there on one train. These cafes are a few minutes' walk from the station.
guides.tips:
*Sample copy.*

- **Go early or late.** Midday is the busiest time around the square.
- **Have a backup.** If the first cafe is full, the next one is a block away.
- **Walk afterwards.** The farmers market runs several days a week and makes a good second stop.

Unsure which spot is quickest for both of you? Compare each trip first and pick the place where the longer trip is shortest.

places.label: Joe Coffee on Union Square West
places.note: Sample note. Steps from the station, so it's an easy landmark when you arrive from different lines.

places.label: Blue Dove Coffee
places.note: Sample note. Another option on the west side of the square if the first stop is too busy to find a table.

places.label: Maman on University Place
places.note: Sample note. A slightly quieter spot a few blocks south, good when the catch-up turns into a longer conversation.

seo.title: A weekend afternoon in Bryant Park with friends
seo.description: Sample guide: how a small group of friends can spend a free weekend afternoon around Bryant Park, with easy subway trips from every borough.

guides.intro:
*Sample copy for local development.*

A weekend plan for a few friends works best when nobody spends half of it on the train. Bryant Park is a short walk from stations on most subway lines, it costs nothing to sit down, and the library next door gives you somewhere to go if the weather turns.
guides.tips:
*Sample copy.*

## Before you go

1. **Check weekend service.** Lines change on weekends, so look up each trip on the day.
2. **Pick a meeting point.** The fountain on the west side is easy to find.
3. **Plan a rain option.** The library's reading rooms are free and a short walk away.

Want to see each friend's trip side by side? [Plan it on Where2Meet](https://www.where2meet.org/) and let the group vote.

places.label: Bryant Park
places.note: Sample note. Movable chairs and a big lawn suit a group that wants to sit together without booking anything.

places.label: New York Public Library, Stephen A. Schwarzman Building
places.note: Sample note. Free to enter and right next to the park, so it works as a backup when it rains.

towns.name: Midtown

seo.title: Where to meet in Midtown
seo.description: Sample guide: places in Midtown Manhattan for team meetings and welcome lunches, a short walk from Grand Central, Bryant Park and Herald Square.

towns.intro:
*Sample copy for local development.*

Midtown is where many New York offices are, so it's the default for anything work-related. Grand Central, Times Square and Herald Square stations put most of the city within one train, and Bryant Park sits between them as an easy landmark.
towns.transit_notes: *Sample copy.* Grand Central, Times Square and Herald Square stations serve most subway lines, and PATH and commuter trains stop nearby. Streets are busiest from 8 to 10 a.m. and 5 to 7 p.m.

seo.title: Quiet places for a small team meeting in Midtown
seo.description: Sample guide: quiet, low-cost places in Midtown for a small team to meet over a weekday lunch, near stations your whole team can reach.

guides.intro:
*Sample copy for local development.*

A small team that works from home most of the week still needs a place to sit together now and then. In Midtown the hard part isn't finding a venue, it's finding one that's quiet enough to talk and close to a station everyone can reach without two transfers. These places cost little or nothing.
guides.tips:
*Sample copy.*

## Before you go

1. **List where everyone starts.** Someone coming from Jersey City has a different trip from someone in Astoria.
2. **Compare travel times, not distance.** A spot two stops from a major hub often beats one that looks central on a map.

## On the day

- Send the address, the nearest station and a meeting point in one message.
- Bring a charger. Outlets go fast in public spaces.

places.label: New York Public Library, Stephen A. Schwarzman Building
places.note: Sample note. Reading rooms suit a quiet working session, and Grand Central and Bryant Park stations are a short walk away.

places.label: Bryant Park
places.note: Sample note. Movable tables and chairs work for an informal check-in on a mild day, with many subway lines close by.

places.label: Nomadworks on Broadway
places.note: Sample note. A coworking space with bookable rooms when the meeting needs a screen and a door.

seo.title: Bookable rooms for a big team meeting in Midtown
seo.description: Sample guide: rooms in Midtown that a team of seven or more can book for a meeting, with a screen, a door and stations close by.

guides.intro:
*Sample copy for local development.*

Once a team grows past six people, public tables stop working. Everyone needs to hear each other, see the same screen and leave their bags somewhere. In Midtown a bookable room costs more than a cafe, but it saves the first twenty minutes of every meeting.
guides.tips:
*Sample copy.*

- **Book for the hour you'll meet.** A room that's empty at 10 a.m. may be full at lunch.
- **Ask about the screen.** Bring the right adapter, or ask the space to have one ready.
- **Share the room name.** Large buildings have several floors, so send the floor and the room with the address.

places.label: Nomadworks on Broadway
places.note: Sample note. Meeting rooms for bigger groups can be booked by the hour, a short walk from Herald Square station.

places.label: New York Public Library, Stephen A. Schwarzman Building
places.note: Sample note. Not bookable, but a quiet place nearby to wait if part of the team arrives early.

seo.title: A team welcome lunch in Bryant Park
seo.description: Sample guide: welcome a new teammate with a relaxed weekday lunch in Bryant Park, easy to reach from most Midtown offices.

guides.intro:
*Sample copy for local development.*

A welcome lunch should feel easy for the new person, not like another meeting. Bryant Park sits between many Midtown offices, so most of the team can walk there, and the kiosks around the lawn mean everyone picks their own lunch.
guides.tips:
*Sample copy.*

- **Pick a corner early.** Tables near the kiosks fill up by noon.
- **Keep it short.** Forty-five minutes is enough for a first lunch together.
- **Have a rain plan.** The library next door is a short walk away.

places.label: Bryant Park
places.note: Sample note. Kiosks around the lawn let everyone buy their own lunch, and the movable chairs fit a big group.
